monthly_review.summary: This month shows a clear shift toward higher-volume, lower-intensity aerobic development — evidenced by increased weekly km, reduced average HR, and a major zone distribution shift toward Z1/Z2 — though at the cost of some aerobic training effect intensity.
monthly_review.highlight: Zone distribution shifted dramatically from 49% combined Z1+Z2 last month to 79% this month — indicating a deliberate, successful focus on foundational aerobic volume.

goal_tracker.message: You’ve already exceeded last month’s total distance (43.8 km vs. 38.0 km) and matched session count — no additional km or runs are needed to surpass April’s totals.

insights.title: Efficiency dip aligns with slower pace & lower HR
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency declined from 13.66 to 13.35 this month — consistent with the 24-sec/km pace slowdown and 6-bpm HR drop, suggesting recent runs prioritized recovery and volume over neuromuscular engagement.

insights.title: Near-elimination of high-intensity work
insights.body: Z4 dropped from 15% to 2% and Z5 disappeared entirely (4% → 0%), meaning no VO2 max or anaerobic stimulus occurred this month — a strategic choice for base-building, but unsustainable long-term without reintroduction.

insights.title: Cadence improved while stride length varied widely
insights.body: Cadence rose +4 spm (142 → 146), yet stride length ranged from 67.6 cm (5.6 km easy run) to 94.4 cm (2.5 km faster effort) — revealing strong context-dependent form adaptation, but also potential inefficiency at slower paces due to overstriding when fatigued.

insights.title: Consistent aerobic load despite pace variability
insights.body: All five recent runs show aerobic TE between 2.4–3.2, confirming steady, manageable load — even the 2.5 km run at 7:27 min/km (447 sec/km) delivered TE 3.2, reflecting appropriate HR response (148 bpm) for your current fitness.

recommendations.action: Do one 45-min Zone 2 run (HR 128–138 bpm) at consistent cadence ≥148 spm, focusing on minimizing vertical oscillation (<7.6 cm) — use your May 20 run (7.5 cm VO, 151 spm) as form reference.
recommendations.reason: Your cadence is trending up and VO is stable (~7.7 cm); reinforcing low-oscillation mechanics at Z2 will improve efficiency without increasing load.

recommendations.action: Insert one 6-km progression run: first 3 km @ Z2 (HR ≤138 bpm), final 3 km @ upper Z3 (HR 147–152 bpm), targeting avg pace ≤520 sec/km (8:40 min/km).
recommendations.reason: Z3 contribution fell from 26% to 19% and Z4 vanished — this safely reintroduces threshold stimulus while staying within your proven HR capacity (May 16 hit 148 bpm at 447 sec/km).

recommendations.action: After your next run, perform 3 × 1-min barefoot strides on grass (soft surface), focusing on landing midfoot directly under hips — aim for ground contact time ≤295 ms (your best recent value was 286 ms on May 16).
recommendations.reason: Ground contact time improved from 309 ms (May 13) to 286 ms (May 16) during a faster effort — this drill reinforces neuromuscular efficiency gains you’re already achieving.

weekly_focus.description: Strengthen the link between your growing aerobic base and efficient movement patterns — preserving endurance gains while sharpening form and readiness for future intensity.
suggested_sessions: Easy 5-km Z1/Z2 run + post-run barefoot strides
